rationale.conceptual: The method involves applying known equations (Clausius-Mossotti, Kramers-Kronig, absorption formula) to DFT-computed polarizabilities. While not novel, it requires careful understanding and correct implementation of these steps, especially the Kramers-Kronig transform and unit conversions. This is an established but non-trivial method in computational spectroscopy.
rationale.execution: The pipeline includes geometry building, three separate DFT polarizability runs (monomer PBE, monomer B3LYP, dimer PBE) across many frequencies, followed by data post-processing in Python. This constitutes a multi-stage workflow with inter-step dependencies, tooling with NWChem and Python libraries, but no particularly fragile or massive orchestration.
